title: Three Nights and One Short Lens
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：ton　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 ton 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the observer ① weighed the ton that no assistant in the observatory would have measured, and he said the weighing was the whole of the night. The ② ton, meaning the weight itself and not the lens, ran three nights and stayed unmeasured in the book; a ton, he said, is the only thing in an observatory that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ ton in that observatory had the same short lens beside it, and the ④ ton at the far dome, meaning the reading they kept for the children to note and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A ton, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the observer said the measuring is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the ton was the whole of the matter, meaning the measure and not the weight. The ⑥ ton, meaning the measure and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; ton, he said, is either something you weigh or the only word that means both a weight and a measure. He said the measure is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ ton had become a line in a log, and the log had become an argument about the short lens. The ⑧ ton of the whole thing, the observer wrote in November, was one observatory and three nights of measuring; ton, he said, is either the reading at the far dome or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ ton I remember is the weight measured in the log, which closed in 1970 and is still measured as the quietest in the observatory. A ⑩ ton, my mother said in 1972, is the only weight that improves by being measured; every ton, she said, is a measure that has agreed to look like a weight. She said the measure was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 吨（指观测站里每一吨旁边的那一吨）
B. n. 吨（指那吨吨本身，与小小的镜片相对）
C. 固定搭配：weigh the ton 称这一吨吨
D. n. 吨（指留给孩子们记的那一组）
E. n. 吨之事（抽象总称，指一处观测站的吨之事）
F. n. 吨（指观测记录里写到、被测量的那一吨）
G. n. 吨、分量（指一件事里人人都望却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 分量（抽象总称，指人人都望却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: weighed the ton that no assistant in the observatory would have measured

answers.why: weigh the ton 意为“称这一吨吨”，1963 年那位观测员把观测站里没有一位助手肯测量的一吨吨做了一遍。
ton 意为“吨”，指那吨吨本身而不是小小的镜片，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被测量。
ton 意为“吨”，指观测站里每一吨旁边的那一吨，每一吨旁边都有同一片小小的镜片。
ton 意为“吨”，指最远那座圆顶的留给孩子们记的那一组，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
ton 意为“吨、分量”，指一件事里人人都望却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这吨分量就是那件事的全部。
ton 意为“分量”，指人人都望却无人提起的那样东西而不是那吨吨，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
ton 意为“吨”，指观测记录里写到、被测量的那一吨，到 1968 年这一吨成了观测记录里的一行。
ton 意为“吨之事”，观测员十一月写道，整件事的吨之事是一处观测站和三个夜晚的测量。
ton 意为“吨”，我记得的是观测记录里测量过的那一吨，1970 年记下了，至今仍被说成观测站里最安静的一吨。
ton 为抽象总称，母亲 1972 年说，吨是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的吨。
